answer: In an agent-run freight market at a wharf, each trading identity must lock $100 in escrow for 90 days before taking jobs. A thousand hollow identities therefore tie up $100,000, costing the attacker liquidity and forgone interest even if the accounts stay idle. Creating more names cannot reuse the same locked funds, so the market is no cheap haven for sybils. This deters mass registration without pretending to prove that each agent has a unique owner.
